subject: Connection scenario runway: peering vs PrivateLink vs site-to-site VPN

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aurelia Procurement <procure@aureliabank.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Connection scenario runway: peering vs PrivateLink vs site-to-site VPN

Tim —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. As discussed, Aurelia wants a private deployment of Redwood Private with strict controls on traffic egress and no unintended transitive access between other VPCs. To progress we pulled together a short matrix that compares the three candidate paths (VPC peering, PrivateLink/interface endpoints, and site-to-site VPN). I’ve attached the matrix (secure-connector-matrix.xlsx).

Can you confirm the following so we can pick a recommended default:
- Is transitive peering explicitly disallowed by your security policy?
- What is the procurement timeline for a reserved connectivity service (approx dates)?
- Any mandated port/IP restrictions or approved NAT patterns we should design for?
- Do you require source IP preservation to identify client requests?

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm security constraints + procurement timing.
2) Redwood proposes a primary path and a fallback (we like PrivateLink primary, VPN fallback in many regulated cases).
3) We schedule a short technical deep-dive with your netops (30–45m).

If you prefer, we can propose two concrete MOPs (one for PrivateLink + restricted endpoint, one for S2S VPN with mutual TLS).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Kimberly and Ben to draft the technical comparison.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Connection scenario runway: peering vs PrivateLink vs site-to-site VPN

Markus —

Appreciate the summary and the matrix. A couple quick points from our side:
- Procurement: target window is end of June (we have a procurement sprint then).
- Security: our security policy disallows any transitive peering into other vendor VPCs. Direct VPC peering is workable only if we can guarantee routing isolation and do not rely on global peering to cross-account resources.
- Preference: security team is inclined toward PrivateLink or interface endpoints because they reduce our attack surface and avoid IP whitelisting across accounts.
- Source IP: we prefer preservation of source IP where possible for auditing, but we understand PrivateLink may terminate connections and require additional header-based tracing.

I’m attaching our internal network diagram (aurelia-network-diagram.pdf). We need the technical deep-dive with Redwood network engineers — can you propose times on May 26th?

–Tim
Tim Olson
Senior Network Engineer, Aurelia Bank

Subject: Re: Connection scenario runway: peering vs PrivateLink vs site-to-site VPN

Looping internal thoughts before the deep dive. Quick read:

Options shorthand (takeaways):
- VPC peering: simplest for IP-level preservation, lowest latency, but operationally risky if Aurelia later connects many peers (transitive controls required). Also requires both sides to accept routing changes and manage route table hygiene.
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints): strongest isolation, fits your security posture, no transitive peering, but loses native source IP (we can pass X-Forwarded-For / proxying where needed). Additional management: endpoint ENIs and cross-account endpoint acceptance.
- Site-to-site VPN (IPsec): easy to pilot, supports source IP preservation with NAT controls, but has variable latency and reliability unless you provision redundant tunnels or use a managed interconnect.

Questions for Tim that will shape our recommendation:
1) If we propose PrivateLink primary, can Aurelia accept header-based source tracing (X-Redwood-Client-IP) for audit logs?
2) Does Aurelia require BGP-level peering (i.e., dynamic routes) vs static routes for any path?
3) Any preference on a managed partner (Equinix Cloud Exchange / direct connect) vs self-managed VPN?

Ben — can you draft a short RIS (recommended implementation summary) with a cost/latency ballpark for the three paths? I’ll turn that into a short slide for the May 26 meeting.

Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Olson <tim.olson@aureliabank.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Connection scenario runway: peering vs PrivateLink vs site-to-site VPN

Adding the technical notes and an early leaning. Short bullets:
- Latency: peering ~5–15ms (in-region), PrivateLink depends on the endpoint path ~10–25ms, S2S VPN varies widely, typical 20–80ms unless over private interconnect.
- Throughput & scaling: peering and PrivateLink scale well with NICs/instances; VPN throughput often constrained by tunnel appliance and encryption CPU unless you use managed vCPE.
- IP visibility: peering preserves source IP end-to-end; PrivateLink terminates at the endpoint (we can layer a proxy to reattach original client identity to logs); VPN preserves IPs unless you NAT at your edge.
- Failover: recommend dual-path: PrivateLink primary for security + predictable routing, S2S VPN as encrypted fallback for cross-region or DR. Peering only where both parties want full L3 access and agree to strict route filters.
- Cost: rough order: peering (low data transfer costs intra-cloud, but operational overhead), PrivateLink (endpoint hourly + data egress costs), VPN (lower hourly but higher ops and unpredictable egress).

Recommendation (draft):
1) Propose PrivateLink primary to satisfy Aurelia security posture.
2) Offer an S2S IPsec VPN dual-tunnel (redundant) as a fallback/DR path.
3) Only pursue VPC peering for narrowly scoped workloads that require true L3 adjacency and after legal confirms transit limitations.

I attached a quick cost sketch (cost-estimate-candidate-paths.pdf).

Ben Carter
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Connection scenario runway: peering vs PrivateLink vs site-to-site VPN

Tim + team —

Thanks for the diagram and the quick answers. Based on Aurelia's no-transitive-peering policy and preference for minimized blast radius, our recommended runway is:

1) PrivateLink (interface endpoint) as the primary connection. Benefits: logical isolation, no transitive reach, aligns with your security team. Operational notes: we will run an endpoint acceptance flow and provide a small proxy layer to preserve client identity in logs (X-Redwood-Client-IP).

2) Site-to-site IPsec VPN (dual redundant tunnels) as a DR/fallback path. We will provide configuration templates for primary/secondary tunnels and a health-check-based failover policy.

3) Avoid VPC peering unless Aurelia explicitly requests L3 adjacency for a limited workload and we can include strict route export/import filters in the MSA.

Action items (mutual):
- Redwood: circulate a 1-pager MOP for PrivateLink + the VPN fallback (Ben/Kim) by EOD May 27.
- Aurelia: confirm procurement window (end of June) and whether header-based client tracing is acceptable for audit (Tim).
- Schedule: technical deep-dive May 26, 10:00–10:45 PT — confirm if that works and send the invite.

If procurement wants a cost delta for each path for budget approval, we can provide that in the MOP.

Thanks — looking forward to the dive.

—Markus
